details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> cuda : use MMVF for BF16 matrices of few rows at small batch sizes (#31959) MMF tiles 32 rows per block, so a BF16 matrix with few rows (e.g. the qwen4exp hyper-connection projections, 320 rows with K = 10240) runs only a handful of blocks and leaves most SMs idle at batch sizes 2..8. MMVF runs a block per row and wins there when K is long enough. MMVF's cost grows with rows x batch while MMF's stays roughly flat in that range, so use MMVF only while rows * ne11 * 256 <= nsm * min(K, max_k) and K >= 1024. The budget scales with the SM count, which keeps GPUs with few SMs (e.g. the A16) on MMF. Blackwell allows up to 8 columns and max_k = 6144; older GPUs stop at 5 columns and max_k = 4096. Add eval cases at 128x2560, 512x2560 and 320x10240 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8. </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/66387378> **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.
